content: (The sentiment of the world is that it and its parts are always waterlessly hunting. What happens when we imagine the Internet is that it is the working of the waterless hunting of the world. But we think of actually imagining sentimentally as if it works like something else, some smaller part of the world that goes against the grain of the sentiment of the world as if it is the catching and burnishing of the corner parts of the world which attract soil and become dirty. Imagining is imagined to be clean and cornerless, like the line between one and the other when we think of a thing working like something else. We say that termites are eusocial in that they work together, and we imagine that the clean and waterless hunting of the Internet might also actually be a form of working together, but I don’t want the analogy of the way termites work to come across and wash away this always there sentiment of the way the world is always waterlessly hunting and replace it with the sense of the time and place of the world where clean water meets and permeates the corner parts of the world, which we say is called a petrichor, and I imagine sadly how a petrichor might have a kind of lifespan, in that it is there at first with a time and place but eventually it runs out.)
title: Net fruiting
